chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who accused his wife of adultery, so they performed li'an (mutual imprecation), and then he accused her again after they had separated, also with adultery. Upon him is a fixed punishment. He said, 'Yes, upon him is a fixed punishment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an if a husband accuses his wife again after separation?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a specific jurisprudential nuance: the husband remains liable for the hadd of qadhf (80 lashes) even if he re-accuses his wife after the li'an process has already dissolved the marriage. This ruling underscores that the initial li'an serves primarily to establish lineage and effect divorce, rather than absolving the accuser of the penalty for false testimony if the accusation persists or is repeated. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct legal consequences of li'an versus standard qadhf.
